steps.title: Beck Cognitive Triad
steps.tx: **Beck cognitive triad of depression** conceptualizes depressive pathology as emerging from pervasive negative core schemas regarding the self ('I am fundamentally defective'), the ongoing world experience ('the entire world is excessively demanding'), and the future ('my personal future is completely hopeless'). These latent dysfunctional cognitive schemas become activated during stressful life events, generating automatic negative thoughts.

steps.title: Identifying Cognitive Distortions
steps.tx: **Common cognitive distortion categories** represent systematic logical errors that reinforce maladaptive schemas: arbitrary inference involves jumping to negative conclusions without supporting proof, dichotomous thinking categorizes situations into absolute all-or-nothing extremes, and overgeneralization extracts a universal rule from an isolated negative incident. Patients track these errors using structured dysfunctional thought records.

steps.title: Socratic Questioning and Restructuring
steps.tx: **Socratic questioning in cognitive restructuring** employs collaborative empiricism, wherein the therapist and patient act as investigative co-scientists. Instead of debating the patient, the clinician poses targeted open-ended questions that gently uncover logical inconsistencies in irrational beliefs, enabling the patient to evaluate objective counter-evidence and independently formulate rational, balanced alternative thoughts.

steps.title: Systematic Desensitisation Principles
steps.tx: **Joseph Wolpe systematic desensitization** is grounded in classical conditioning and reciprocal inhibition, postulating that an individual cannot simultaneously experience physiological relaxation and psychological fear. Patients construct an anxiety stimulus hierarchy ranging from mild discomfort to extreme dread, progressively confronting each fear tier while maintaining profound muscular relaxation until the conditioned anxiety response extinguishes.

steps.title: Exposure and Response Prevention
steps.tx: **Exposure and response prevention protocol** stands as the definitive first-line behavioural intervention for obsessive-compulsive disorder. The patient is exposed systematically to distressing obsession-provoking environmental triggers (such as touching contaminated floor tiles) while strictly refraining from executing habitual anxiety-reducing compulsive rituals (such as repetitive hand washing), driving neurological extinction and habituation.

steps.title: Operant Conditioning and Token Economy
steps.tx: **Token economy behavioural modification** applies Skinnerian operant conditioning principles within institutional psychiatric wards, rehabilitation facilities, and specialized classrooms. Patients earn secondary reinforcers, such as plastic tokens or reward points, immediately upon performing target adaptive behaviors (personal hygiene, room maintenance, group participation), which are subsequently exchanged for desired primary privileges.

steps.title: Aversion Therapy versus Flooding
steps.tx: **Aversion therapy and flooding techniques** utilize contrasting conditioning models: aversion therapy couples an undesirable maladaptive habit with an intensely noxious stimulus, such as administering emetic apomorphine or disulfiram with alcohol, or bitter nail paint for onychophagia. Flooding involves immediate, sustained immersion in the most frightening phobic situation without gradual hierarchical steps until autonomic exhaustion forces extinction.

steps.title: Jacobson Progressive Relaxation
steps.tx: **Jacobson progressive muscle relaxation** instructs patients to systematically tense specific muscle groups for 5 to 7 seconds, followed by sudden complete release for 20 to 30 seconds, traversing 16 major anatomical muscle regions. This exercise cultivates somatic awareness of muscular tension, enabling patients to extinguish sympathetic arousal during panic attacks, generalized anxiety, and tension headaches.
